F1.quote: For the poet nicknamed the Prince of Poets, see Ahmed Shawqi. For the French distinction, see Prince des poètes.
F1.claim: the article's own disambiguation: the phrase also names Shawqi's epithet and the French distinction

F2.quote: Prince of Poets is a reality television poetry competition on the Emirati television network Abu Dhabi TV.

F3.quote: It was created in April 2007 by the Abu Dhabi Authority for Culture and Heritage, and airs live from the Al Raha Beach theatre every week.
F3.claim: created April 2007 by the Abu Dhabi Authority for Culture and Heritage; live from Al Raha Beach

F4.quote: The winner is awarded one million dirhams and a symbolic cloak and ring.
F4.claim: the prize: one million dirhams, a symbolic cloak and ring
F4.lineage: the awarded title and its cloak

F5.quote: Reflecting the pre-eminence of poetry in the Arab world, the programme's ratings overtook those of football and of other reality television programmes, with a studio audience of thousands and a television audience of millions.
F5.claim: ratings above football and other reality programmes

F6.quote: Its title comes from the epithet of Arabic-language epic poet Ahmed Shawqi.
F6.claim: the program's title comes from Shawqi's epithet

F7.quote: Thousands of aspiring poets from all over the Arab world submit their poems, and several dozen are chosen to compete.

F8.quote: In the competition, contestants read their poems, and are also asked to improvise poems on various subjects. … A jury of established poets and critics judges and offers feedback on the entries, while the studio audience and viewers at home can also vote for their preferred poets.
F8.claim: recital and improvisation; a jury of poets and critics; audience vote

F9.quote: Despite the show's title, the contestants can be male or female.
F9.claim: contestants of either sex despite the title

F10.quote: Prince of Poets is similar to another Emirati poetry competition, Million's Poet; the latter promotes Nabati (Bedouin) poetry, while the former promotes classical Arabic poetry and is an attempt to revive it in modern society. … Like Million's Poet, it has been compared to American Idol.
F10.claim: beside Million's Poet: classical Arabic poetry, an attempt to revive it; compared to American Idol

F11.quote: Egyptian poet Hisham al Gakh was an audience favorite in the competition's fourth season after presenting a controversial poem, "The Visa," which criticized Arab leaders. … he came in second after Yemeni poet Abdul Aziz al Zera'i.
F11.claim: season four: Hisham al Gakh's 'The Visa'; second to Abdul Aziz al Zera'i

F12.quote: Palestinian poet Tamim al-Barghouti competed in the first season. Although he finished the competition in fifth place, he became very popular among Palestinians
F12.claim: Tamim al-Barghouti, first season, fifth, very popular

F13.quote: Other winners have been Syrian Hassan Baiti (third season), … Mauritanian Sidi Mohamed Ould Bamba (second season), … and Emirati Abdul Kareem Maatouk (first season).

F14.quote: The programme's presenters have included Dhafer L'Abidine, in the first series,

F15.quote: As Abu Dhabi moved towards achieving its goal of becoming a leading regional capital of culture, the TV program “Prince of Poets” was launched in 2007 to put poetry again in the centre of the cultural scene.
F15.claim: launched 2007 to put poetry again at the centre, as Abu Dhabi sought to be a capital of culture

F16.quote: A television program organized by the Cultural and Heritage Programs and Festivals Management Committee in Abu Dhabi, once every two years on Al Raha Beach Theater in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi.
F16.claim: the organizer's definition: organized by the Committee, once every two years, Al Raha Beach

F17.quote: It is a literary competition in the field of eloquent Arabic poetry, the first season of which was launched in 2007 .
F17.claim: a literary competition in eloquent Arabic poetry, first season 2007

F18.quote: Each season, the program receives thousands of poems from Arab poets from all over the world, and the jury sorts and evaluates the participating works, after which more than 1 50 poets who have been selected will be hosted in the capital Abu Dhabi, … Then, the top 40 poets are selected from among the applicants to enter the testing phase, leading to the list of 20 poets who will participate in the program's live episodes.
F18.claim: selection: thousands of poems, some 150 hosted, 40 tested, 20 in the live episodes

F19.quote: At the end of each season, the first-place winner receives the title of "Prince of Poets", the cloak of hair, the seal of the emirate, and a cash prize of one million dirhams,
F19.claim: the awarded title, the cloak of hair, the seal of the emirate, one million dirhams
F19.lineage: the awarded title and its cloak

F20.quote: the second-place winner receives a cash prize of 500 thousand dirhams, and the third-place winner receives 300 thousand
F20.lineage: the awarded title and its cloak

F21.quote: Prince des poètes (French: Prince of poets) is an honorific and unofficial title given in France to French-speaking poets of various nationalities.
F21.claim: the French honorific defined: unofficial, given in France to French-speaking poets

F22.quote: Poets who have held the title include Pierre de Ronsard (16th century), Charles Marie René Leconte de Lisle (1885–1894), Paul Verlaine (1894–1896), Stéphane Mallarmé (1896–1898), Léon Dierx (1898–1912), Paul Fort (1912–1960), Jules Supervielle (1960), Jean Cocteau (1960–1963), Maurice Carême (1972–1978), and Léopold Sédar Senghor (1978–2001).
